customManagers.description: Longhorn is installed with kubectl apply, not Helm or ArgoCD, so no standard manager can see it. Track the version pinned in its README instead — this is the only reason it sat 5 minor versions behind.

packageRules.description: Majors stay off — they need reading, not a PR queue.

Pin every image by digest. A tag (even 'php8.3-apache' or '11.8') is rebuilt in place upstream for security fixes; only a digest makes that rebuild visible as a PR (PHP2Shell 2026-10-22: three WordPress sites sat on a vulnerable PHP for this reason, CLSTR-40).
DEFAULT: digest and patch bumps auto-merge, and so does pinning (same image, digest added). These are the redis/ollama-style updates that drown the important PRs.
Security rebuilds should not wait for the weekend: digest/patch/pin run nightly. Minors and majors keep the weekend schedule.
Remaining minors group into one weekend PR. Placed BEFORE the infra/db rules: Renovate gives later rules precedence, so infra/database minors fall through to their own groups instead of landing here.
Infrastructure NEVER auto-merges — a bad cert-manager or ingress bump locks you out of everything downstream, and ArgoCD auto-syncs whatever lands on main.
Data stores never auto-merge — any image bump restarts the pod, and a restart mid-backup silently produces empty dumps (see the netpol pod-admission lag).
Vaultwarden is manual: it holds every credential plus the SOPS break-glass key. An unattended restart that goes wrong locks you out of the recovery path itself.

LiteLLM is manual: 1.107.0 was a supply-chain compromise (2026-10-21) and the image is pinned by digest only, so an automerged digest bump can swap the release with no version visible in the PR (it did, #107, 2026-10-23).

Longhorn gets its OWN PR, never mixed into the infrastructure group: merging its bump only edits the README pin — the actual upgrade is a manual, sequential-minor kubectl apply. A grouped merge would make the README lie about what is deployed.
